newsitem.title: USA: N.Carolina declares state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: N.Carolina declares state of emergency.

text.p: North Carolina Governor Jim Hunt declared a state of emergency because of Hurricane Fran on Thursday, and said evacuation orders were in effect for more than 500,000 residents and tourists in the state.

"This is a very powerful storm and it is veering toward our coast," Hunt said. "It will come inland apparently in North Carolina, rather than South Carolina, and it is just immense in terms of its width. It is almost going to cover the whole state."
"I am asking everybody to leave those barrier islands, everybody to leave those coastal towns," the governor said.
It was the state of emergency ever declared for all 100 North Carolina counties, Hunt said.
"We've had tremendous flooding in the west. We've had 11 inches (28 cm) of rain in 12 hours. We've got roads washed out, and this is going to come on top of that," Hunt said.

Residents and tourists in five coastal counties were under evacuation orders, emergency officials said. They included popular beach areas near Wilmington and Morehead City and the southern Outer Banks, a string of slender barrier islands. Forecasts said hurricane-force winds and storm surges of up to 15 feet (4.5 metres) could pound much of the state's southeastern area.
